company: Sticker Control (US), Inc. / SC Tech Systems
dod_intent_evidence: AFWERX Phase I and II SBIR awards (Air Force, 2022 PhII $1,249,969) plus a dedicated 'Department of War Work' page describing use across multiple Air Force squadrons (Aircraft Maintenance, Security Forces, Logistics Readiness, Civil Engineering) — see 'Their own words' and 'SBIR/STTR record' sections.
score_evidence: 'Process Automation and Asset Management Solution...with real-time tracking and AI-powered optimization algorithms and data models' → lab_language_intensity (mild buzzword framing, mostly ops-grounded)

'With the real-time views we provide, our customers: Automate manual processes' with zero mention of DDIL/ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/STIG anywhere in site or SBIR abstract → deployment_awareness_absence (capped at 12, own-language word count ~623 <1000)
'Currently Have a Sequential Phase II through OTST - call us about the no-cost use our system under this award' → stage_pressure (active SBIR period-of-performance clock, tiny 3-13 person team)

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Real-time views' and continuous data capture assume live connectivity
blind_spots.operator_reality: At an austere OCONUS site with intermittent comms, 'real-time' asset visibility silently degrades to stale or missing data with no graceful fallback described anywhere in their materials
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product was built and sold around garrison/squadron IT environments, not contested/DDIL field use
blind_spots.evidence_quote: With the real-time views we provide, our customers: Automate manual processes

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/STIG language despite already running on Air Force squadron operations
blind_spots.operator_reality: Software already 'working with multiple Air Force squadrons' but never mentioning an Authority to Operate suggests it may be running informally outside the government network authorization process, a compliance gap that can kill an expansion PoP overnight
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Small commercial software team (3-13 people) unlikely to have in-house ISSO/compliance function
blind_spots.evidence_quote: SC Tech's OPERA™ software system uses digital forms and any type of sensor to make it easy for organizations to capture data in order to have real-time visibility into operations.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Sensor-agnostic hardware (RFID, barcodes, GPS) mounted on field assets with no SWaP-C or battery/sustainment discussion
blind_spots.operator_reality: Field-mounted sensors on aircraft maintenance or logistics equipment need battery logistics, ruggedization, and a sustainment plan for who replaces failed sensors in the field — none of which is addressed
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team framing is enterprise-software-first ('digital forms and sensors') rather than field-hardware-first
blind_spots.evidence_quote: digital forms and sensors (RFID, barcodes, GPS, whatever the context requires) to make it easy for organizations to capture and use data - in the office and in the field

opener_hook: SC Tech's second AFWERX Phase II SBIR (Air Force, $1.25M) is running while OPERA is already live across Aircraft Maintenance, Security Forces, and Logistics Readiness squadrons — how's the ATO conversation going as that footprint grows?
what_they_do: Sensor-agnostic asset tracking and process automation software (OPERA) selling into Air Force squadrons for maintenance, security, and logistics operations.
